title: Quantum capacity of the symmetric platypus channel
source: This is the symmetric member $s=1/2$ of the platypus channels in Section~3.1, Eq.~(20), of Leditzky et al. Their Section~5, Eq.~(70), shows that the spin alignment conjecture would give $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{N})=q_1$ \sourcecite{ref:spq-leditzky}{LLSSS23}.
progress: For the channel in Eq.~\eqref{eq:spq-isometry}, Section~4.1 gives $q_1=\max_{0\leq u\leq1}[h_2(u)+(1-u)-h_2((1-u)/2)]$, with $h_2$ the binary entropy. Section~6.2 proves the two-spin entropy inequality in this symmetric case, which with the reduction in Section~5 yields $q_2=2q_1$. Theorem~3 gives the unconditional capacity upper bound $\log_2(1+1/\sqrt{2})$ \sourcecite{ref:spq-leditzky}{LLSSS23}.

Smith and Wu prove additivity for some generalized platypus channels. In Section~V after Proposition~V.5 they discuss the original $t=0$ family, for which the spin-alignment argument remains conditional \sourcecite{ref:spq-smith-wu}{SW25}.

Song and Chen's three-qubit example violates a stronger spin-alignment majorization conjecture. Their Section~II Remark checks that the example does not violate the original von Neumann entropy inequality. Guo et al. observe a coherent-information gain using the symmetric platypus with a different assisting channel \sourcecite{ref:spq-song-chen}{SC26} \sourcecite{ref:spq-guo}{Guo26}.

comment: The target concerns self-tensor powers of one fixed channel. The \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_a59d7cc1c843edb5/}{exactly solvable nondegradable channel problem} allows the channel to be chosen, while the \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_3ea0de34a1fe6e0b/}{finite truncation problem} quantifies over all channels. The catalog and literature were checked through November 26, 2026.
